 "architecture": "Survival-first design (\"outlive the lobby\"). One decision function, a priority cascade rather than utility scoring, with eight modes: fight, retreat, cover, rotate, hold, loot, supply drop, unstuck. Order each decision: (1) update memory: enemy tracks kept 20 s, damage log 12 s, sounds 8 s, remembered weapon pickups; (2) answer any upgrade offer; (3) pick a target among currently visible mechs by distance, minus 80 m if it hurt us in the last 3 s, minus 40 m if under 400 HP; (4) engagement test: fight if the target is within 55 m, or it attacked us (last 4 s) within 90 m while our HP is above 45%, or it attacked us within 250 m and we hold a laser and have at least 90% of its HP, or it is weak (under 35% HP) within 160 m; a fight at low HP and more than 40 m away becomes a retreat to cover; an attacker outside those ranges triggers cover mode instead; (5) zone urgency overrides everything except a fight with slack; (6) when calm (no enemy within 90 m, not hurt for 3 s) go for loot, else an uncontested supply drop; (7) default is rotate along a flow field then hold a concealed spot. Movement overlays applied afterwards in rising priority: quiet-walk cap, enemy avoidance (v5.4), ducking a charging laser, dodging shells and bullets, stuck recovery. Aim and fire are computed independently of the movement mode, so it shoots while retreating, covering or rotating. All ~45 thresholds live in one parameter block that can be overridden by an environment variable set in the Dockerfile, which is how they pushed one-parameter variant branches to the real scorer as A/B tests. Robustness: a reader thread queues input, only the newest observation is answered and the events, sounds and beams of skipped ones are merged into it; a panic in the decision repeats the last movement with all one-shot actions cleared; runs without a map if loading fails. Timing: about 0.3 ms per decision, p99 about 15 ms because the flow-field slice uses the remaining time up to 14 ms after the observation arrived; ready in about 0.4 s.",
 "navigation": "World model on a 1 m grid aligned with terrain vertices: building prisms scanline-rasterised into per-cell vertical solid intervals; a floor layer per cell (lowest surface with 9 m head-room: terrain, roof or bridge deck; high bridges are walked under, low overhangs are walls). A cell is standable if nothing rising above step height lies within 3.2 m (body radius + 0.7 m). Walking edges are 8-neighbour with step and slope limits and a cost penalty of 35% per cell for cells closer than 4 m to a wall, which keeps paths off walls. Roof access is in the graph: from standable cells touching a wall it probes 16 directions up to 11 m for the first standable cell across the wall band; a higher one (up to 45 m, no overhang underside in the way) becomes a jump+jet edge costing distance + 4 + 1.2 per metre climbed, a lower one becomes a cheap drop edge. Climb execution: stand at the take-off cell until energy is about 1.6 per metre of climb + 8 (no waiting when outside the zone), jump, jet until feet are 0.8 m above the roof, drift onto it, 6 s timeout. Long-range movement is a multi-source Dijkstra distance field seeded from every standable cell in an inner disc of the NEXT circle (60% of its radius; 55% under 80 m; 50% under 30 m; 4 m for the final point), grown by 25% steps if the disc has under 40 standable cells; computed in about 8 time slices (about 120 ms total) and followed by chaining up to 40 next-cell pointers, so knock-backs and detours need no replanning. Short trips (loot, cover, hold spot) use a bounded A* (12,000 expansions, replanned every 1.5 s or when the goal moves 2 m) with straight-line shortcuts when the segment is walkable. Path following is string-pulling to the farthest directly walkable cell among the next 30. Stuck detection compares commanded with actual speed over 1.6 s: stuck when displacement is under 18% of expected (or under 0.8 m) with little height change; recovery is a 0.9 s jump+jet burst in a direction rotated 0, +90, -90, 180 degrees by consecutive stuck count, with jitter; a hold spot that caused it is replaced by the current cell. Nav smoke test: 30/30 runs alive to the final circle, 9 stuck events, longest 5.1 s. Roofs are used only for transit; roof holding was tested and rejected.",
 "aiming_and_fire_control": "Aim point: target body centre at 4.5 m, and if that line is blocked by terrain/buildings, 2 m higher, then 3.6 m higher; the first clear one is used (at range the lower body is often hidden and centre shots hit the ground). Gun: closed-form constant-velocity intercept using the weapon's own projectile speed, with the target's vertical velocity clamped and damped to 30%; latency compensation advances the target by 0.05 s and the own muzzle by own velocity over 0.05 s before solving. Fires when the aim error is within about 2 m at the target's distance plus 0.01 rad, a clear line exists, range is under 98% of max, there is ammo, and the cooldown is zero or will expire inside the coming 0.1 s decision window (trigger held early so the server fires the instant it ends). No gun fire at targets beyond 140 m that move faster than 4 m/s. Laser: charging starts when cooled down and within about 0.35 rad of the target; while charging the torso keeps following the gun lead and the gun keeps firing; at 80% charge the torso switches to the laser aim, which leads the target and own motion by 75 ms; release only when the error is within about 1.6 m at the target and the line is clear; otherwise the charge is held (also when the target disappears), never dumped. Lightning: aim straight at the target once within range + 8 m; fire inside range - 1 m and within 85% of the half-cone, if energy covers the shot. Mortar: 22-230 m only, ballistic solve iterated three times for target lead, low arc with a clear line and high arc over buildings without one, fires within 0.03 rad of the solution. Reload: no tactical reload; tops up only when no target exists and the magazine is under half (a reload-behind-cover option tested neutral). Not engaged: face the target, else the last damage bearing, else a sound under 2 s old, else scan (sweep +-60 degrees around the heading while moving so the 120 degree view covers about 240; +-70 degrees around the open side when backed against a wall; slow full rotation otherwise). Crates are shot with the gun when calm.",
 "survival_and_anti_squad_tactics": "Core plan against the squad is to avoid and hide, and fight only close or when attacked. (a) Concealed hold spots: after reaching the next-circle disc, breadth-first search of cells reachable on foot within 45 m; pre-score by wall proximity (best at 2-3 m), canopy overhead, short walk and centrality; the best 60 plus a spread sample of 40 are tested against 16 distant viewpoints (8 directions at 70 and 120 m, eye height) using buildings, terrain and exact foliage chord length (about 4 m of crown blocks sight beyond 45 m); each hidden viewpoint adds score. The spot stores the direction away from nearby walls and the torso sweeps only that sector so the 1.5x rear arc faces the wall. (b) Quiet movement: speed capped at 40% while holding or looting when an enemy is within 80 m or near footsteps were heard in the last 4 s; the final 25 m to a hold spot is walked at 42%. (c) Cover from far attackers: 72 candidate points (24 directions at 12, 22, 34 m) scored for no line of sight from each threat, distance from threats and reachability; it stays 8 s after the last hit so the 5 s regen delay elapses, then picks a new hold spot instead of returning to the exposed one; an unseen shooter is placed 120 m along the damage bearing. It shoots back while moving to cover. (d) Retreat to cover below 45% HP when the enemy is more than 40 m away, boosting if energy is above 40; with no cover it keeps strafing. (e) Fight movement: strafe perpendicular with a random left/right re-roll every 0.8-2.0 s, drift to a preferred range of 60 m gun-only, 90 m with laser, 80 m mortar, 30 m lightning; no boost strafing. (f) Peek-fighting laser carriers at 35-260 m: sample points within 13 m, pair a spot hidden from the enemy's eye with an exposed spot 2-6.5 m from it; hide while the enemy charges, while the own laser is still charging, or when below 30% HP and behind on HP; step out during the enemy cooldown, and step out anyway before the own charge would auto-fire into the wall. Separately, any visible enemy charging a laser whose aim passes within about 6 m of us (beyond 30 m) triggers a boosted dash to the hidden spot. (g) Dodging: integrate mortar shells to impact and leave splash radius + 3.5 m; sidestep bullets whose closest approach is under 3 m in 0.12-0.8 s, boosting if energy is above 25. (h) Blind return fire: beam origins and damage bearings create inferred targets that are shot through trees. (i) v5.4 avoidance: while holding, rotating or looting, add a repulsion from every enemy seen in the last 15 s within 200 m that is not currently attacking, plus sound-located threats (footsteps assumed at 30 m, near gunfire/laser at 40 m, mid at 100 m, last 3 s), never moving toward a threat and never leaving the zone; hold-spot scoring also penalises cells near enemies seen in the last 20 s. There is no specific plan for the single early hunter (the solo-duel option that fights a lone attacker head-on down to 25% HP is off after testing) and no late-game answer to the whole squad hunting beyond hiding and tracking the circle.",
 "loot_weapons_upgrades": "Weapon preference laser > lightning > mortar, and slot 1 is swapped only for a higher-ranked weapon. Weapon pickups seen once are remembered for up to 150 s (forgotten when within 30 m without seeing them, or after a take). Looting happens only when calm, for items within 70 m, within 8 m of the bot's height and inside the zone 15 s ahead; score is distance minus 15 m per weapon rank; cubes within 60 m score distance minus 10 m. A loot goal not reached in 14 s is blacklisted for 60 s; a failed take is blacklisted for 20 s. Crates within 70 m are shot with the gun until 240 s when no mech has been seen for 3 s and no damage taken for 6 s. NPC drones are ignored by default: both farming and shooting back at drones are switchable but off after tests. Supply drops are opportunistic: only one landing within 6 s (or landed), within 90 m, not held by another mech, no enemy within 110 m of it, inside the zone; the bot stands within 3 m of its centre. Upgrade choice is a fixed list: plating, armor, nanites first; then lightning efficiency, laser charge, laser damage, lightning range if the weapon is held; then gun rate, gun damage, sensors, mortar reload, gyros, servos, gun magazine, capacitor, jets, reactor, gun velocity, and the remaining weapon perks last. Optional and off: collecting drops near own kills from farther away (tested neutral or negative).",
 "zone_and_endgame": "Rotates early toward the NEXT circle via the flow field and holds inside its inner 50-60% disc. Urgency: outside the zone now, or walking time to the disc plus 10 s exceeds the predicted time until the current position falls outside (edge predicted from the shrink schedule in 1 s steps up to 90 s ahead, 4 m margin). When urgent: rotate, boost if outside or with under 3 s of slack and energy above 15; a fight is abandoned for running (still shooting) when slack is under 4 s. Fight strafing is bent back toward the zone if the point 15 m ahead would be outside 5 s later. Loot, cover and avoidance targets must stay inside the future zone. Final phase (next radius about zero): only the moving centre is safe, so it walks to where the centre will be 1.5 s ahead with 0.3 m precision, slowing as it closes; during a fight when the current radius is under 40 m it stops strafing and moves to that point whenever it is more than about a third of the radius from it. The flow field seeds grow automatically when the circle sits on roofs or off the map. No other endgame logic.",
 "housebot_observations": "From their recorded practice stream and duel traces (real scorer): practice behaves as a duel test, one hunter at first, more as hunters die, all of them late; squad bots do not kill each other, so score is about the number of hunters that die before the bot. The house hunter arrives already carrying gun + laser, fights at 100-150 m and never closes inside 45 m, so lightning never gets used against it. The hunter killed them through tree canopy (trees stop sight, not shots) while they could not see it. Re-running one build gave 3.75, 3.90, 3.67. Their sim model of the squad (assumptions, not measurements): hunters always know the bot's position, weakest grade hunts first, lasers only on the stronger grades, everyone hunts after 300 s. Sim-only death diagnostics in that model: 82% of deaths had 2+ distinct attackers in the last 10 s, lasers did 60-69% of the killing damage, the first hit came at a median 9-17 s, about 77% of deaths occurred while retreating, and rear hits were 10-14% of damage taken.",

 "novel_ideas": [
  "Hold the trigger whenever a weapon's cooldown will end within the next decision interval; applied to gun, laser charge start, lightning and mortar.",
  "Aim-point ladder: body centre, then +2 m, then +3.6 m, taking the first with a clear line from the muzzle.",
  "Two-weapon aim sharing: follow the gun lead while the laser charges, switch the torso to the laser solution at 80% charge with a short release lead, release only on target, hold the charge otherwise, and step out of cover before the forced auto-release.",
  "Latency compensation on both ends: advance the target and the own muzzle by about half a decision before solving the intercept.",
  "Inferred targets: a laser or lightning beam's start point gives the shooter's muzzle position; a damage bearing plus last known (or weapon-typical) distance gives an estimate; fire at them through foliage since only buildings and terrain stop shots.",
  "Peek pairs: precompute a hidden spot and an exposed spot a few metres apart and alternate between them on the enemy laser's charge/cooldown cycle while pre-charging the own laser in cover.",
  "Duck test for incoming lasers: enemy flagged as charging and its aim yaw within the angle subtended by about 6 m at our range.",
  "Hold-spot concealment score from 16 far viewpoints with exact foliage chord length, plus a remembered open direction so the torso sweeps only the exposed sector and the rear arc faces a wall.",
  "Flow field seeded from the whole inner disc of the next circle, time-sliced across decisions and followed by pointer chaining; the seed disc grows when the circle has too little standable ground.",
  "Roof climbs and drops as weighted edges in the same graph, with an energy wait before take-off.",
  "Sound-based avoidance: convert footsteps and gunfire bands into assumed-distance threats and steer away while not fighting.",

  "Inferred targets count as visible for only one decision (0.15 s freshness), so blind return fire happens only on decisions in which a new hit or beam arrives.",
